messages:
aj: Heads up — canary deploys failing in CI for the last 10 mins. Error looks like service-account impersonation failure: `invalid_grant: Token used too early (nbf)`. Pasted build log below.

ci-bot: deploy/canary #1234 FAILED — exit code 1

aj: log snippet:
```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{"error":"invalid_grant","error_description":"Token used too early (nbf claim)"}
```

maria: did we roll something on the OIDC provider? nbf errors usually mean clock skew or token issuance time ahead of runner time.

samir: ^ also could be token lifetime/ttl issue if the runner requests a token with a future iat. Which runner image? self-hosted or cloud?

aj: self-hosted linux runners in eu-west-1. date shows `Thu Mar 14 12:43:10 UTC 2026` on a failing host. The token `iat` in payload is `1700003000` which is 3m ahead.

maria: can you paste how CI exchanges OIDC? are we using short-lived tokens via `sts:token_exchange` or a custom flow?

aj: we call internal endpoint `POST /oidc/exchange` that requests token from idp with `aud=redwood-ci` and then uses it to call `POST /v1/iam:impersonate` -> error. Minimal repro below:
```
# simulate exchange
curl -s -X POST https://idp.example.com/token -d 'grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange&aud=redwood-ci' | jq .
# returns access_token with iat 1700003000
```

samir: two immediate checks:
1) verify host clock against NTP (run `chronyc sources || ntpstat`) on the runner.
2) check the OIDC provider's clock skew tolerance/nbf leeway — some idps allow 2-5 min.

maria: also check the CI runner image build — we recently bumped to alpine:3.18 which shipped `chrony` removed? maybe ntp not running.

aj: running `chronyc tracking` shows NTP unreachable on the host; network egress blocked by firewall rule from the subnet. Opening a temporary egress rule fixed time and the deploy succeeded for a single run.

aj: but we need a durable fix. Thoughts on least-privilege changes while we fix clocks? We don't want to give long-lived keys.

samir: options:
- Re-enable NTP/chrony on runners (preferred) — config + infra ticket.
- Add small clock leeway on identity provider (2m) — risk: increases acceptance of slightly skewed tokens.
- As a mitigation, make CI request tokens with `iat` explicitly set to now (if library allows) or delay few seconds before using token.

maria: for least privilege, make sure the CI service principal only has `iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken` and `iam.serviceAccounts.impersonate` on the specific SA, not project-wide. Example IAM grant (gcloud style):
```
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding redwood-prod \  --member=serviceAccount:ci-runner@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com \  --role=roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator \  --condition=None
```

aj: we had roles applied at folder-level previously, will tighten.

opsbot: ticket created: INF-2109 — "CI runners: enable NTP + tighten SA bindings" (assigned to infra)

samir: also check token exchange code — if using JWT library ensure `leeway=120` when verifying `nbf` on the consuming side.

aj: taking action:
- opened INF-2109, adding infra and security.
- temporary egress rule to NTP restored time and one successful canary deploy.
- rolling update of self-hosted runner images to include chrony.

maria: minor note: make sure we don't widen SA roles for the quick fix. Do NOT create long-lived keys. Use impersonation.

aj: agreed. Will post back once the runner image rollout completes.

(13 minutes later)

aj: update — runners rolled, NTP reachable, no more `nbf` errors in last 30 runs. Canary passed. Closing for now; keeping INF-2109 open for policy cleanup.

ci-bot: deploy/canary #1238 SUCCEEDED :tada:

aj: thanks everyone. tagging @maria for any follow-up security review.
